title: Nineteen Expeditions and One Unopened Case
subtitle: 探索与发现 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 探索与发现（宇宙探索·探索与发现）
meta: 主题语境：探索与发现（宇宙探索·探索与发现）　|　核心词汇：discovery　|　正文 338 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 discovery 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1948 the explorer ① made a discovery that no society in the capital would have credited, and he said the making was the whole of the expedition. The ② discovery, meaning the finding and not the find, ran nineteen expeditions and stayed unopened in the case; a discovery, he said, is the only thing in an expedition that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ discovery in that case had the same unopened box beside it, and the ④ discovery at the end, meaning the one they kept for the maps and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever described twice. A discovery, his assistant said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to make; the explorer said the patience is the part that fills nineteen expeditions.

The curator meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the discovery was the whole of the collection, meaning the find and not the finding. The ⑥ discovery, meaning the find and not any of that, is the only thing in a collection that everybody labels and nobody studies; discovery, she said, is either something you make or the only word that means both a finding and a find. She said the find is the part they remember.

By 1956 the ⑦ discovery had become a line in a journal, and the journal had become an argument about the unopened box. The ⑧ discovery of the whole thing, the explorer wrote in June, was one case and nineteen expeditions of describing; discovery, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to describe. She said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ discovery I remember is the one at the end, which was published in 1970 and is still described as the strangest in the case. A ⑩ discovery, the assistant said in 1972, is the only thing that improves by being studied; every discovery, she said, is a find that has agreed to look like a finding. She said the find was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 发现（指考察中作出的那一项）
B. n. 发现（指那个发现行为本身，与那件发现物相对）
C. 固定搭配：make a discovery 作出一项发现
D. n. 发现（指留给地图用的那一项）
E. n. 发现；发现之事（抽象总称，指一只箱子里的全部发现）
F. n. 发现（指期刊上写到、被发表的那一项）
G. n. 发现物；被发现的事物（指藏品里被贴上标签的那件）
H. n. 发现物（抽象总称，指人人贴标签却无人研究的那些）

items.q: made a discovery that no society in the capital would have credited
The discovery, meaning the finding and not the find
the discovery was the whole of the collection
the discovery had become a line in a journal
The discovery of the whole thing
A discovery, the assistant said in 1972

answers.why: make a discovery 意为“作出一项发现”，1948 年探险家作出了一项首都没有一家学会肯承认的发现。
discovery 意为“发现”，指那个发现行为本身而不是那件发现物，它历经十九次考察而始终没有描述。
discovery 意为“发现”，指那只箱子里每一项发现，每一项旁边都有同一只未开启的盒子。
discovery 意为“发现”，指留给地图用的那一项，是唯一有人描述过两次的。
discovery 意为“发现物、被发现的事物”，指藏品里被贴上标签的那件，馆长说这些发现物就是那批藏品的全部。
discovery 意为“发现物”，指人人贴标签却无人研究的那些而不是那个发现行为，是藏品里人人都贴标签、却无人研究的那些。
discovery 意为“发现”，指期刊上写到、被发表的那一项，到 1956 年这项发现成了期刊里的一行。
discovery 意为“发现、发现之事”，探险家六月写道，整件事的发现是一只箱子和十九次考察的描述。
discovery 意为“发现”，我记得的是末尾那一项，1970 年发表，至今仍被说成箱子里最奇的一项。
discovery 为抽象总称，助手 1972 年说，一项发现是唯一会因为被研究而变得更好的东西。
